findings.problem: The proof that the center of S is trivial, for S ≅ E6(K) adjoint, repeats in at least five proofs across four files. It applies `center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup` and then discharges the multiplier hypothesis with the same lines. Those lines obtain `e6_hopfMultiplier hK5`, rewrite `Nat.card_congr eM.toEquiv`, `Nat.card_congr Multiplicative.toAdd` and `Nat.card_zmod`, and then argue about `Nat.gcd 3 (Nat.card K - 1)`. Only the last divisibility step differs between copies. The same non-trivial reasoning (the Hopf multiplier of E6 has order gcd(3, |K|-1)) is pasted each time, so any change to the multiplier API or to `center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup` has to be made in every copy.
findings.proposed_change:
Next to `center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup` in S267BadExcHRConc.lean, add an E6-specific lemma:

theorem center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup_E6 {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hperf : ⁅S, S⁆ = S) (hcore : GLAPPrimeCore p ↥S = ⊥) {K : Type} [Field K] [Finite K] (eX : ↥(adjointGroup .E6 K) ≃* PSimple p S) (hK5 : 5 ≤ Nat.card K) (hM : ¬ p ∣ Nat.gcd 3 (Nat.card K - 1)) : Subgroup.center ↥S = ⊥ := center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup hp hperf hcore eX (by obtain ⟨-, ⟨eM⟩⟩ := CFSG.LieType.Steinberg.CentralExt.MinusculeClosed.e6_hopfMultiplier hK5; rw [Nat.card_congr eM.toEquiv, Nat.card_congr Multiplicative.toAdd, Nat.card_zmod]; exact hM)

The rewritten uses are:
- Target file: `have hZ := center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup_E6 Nat.prime_three hperf hcore eX hK5 (fun h => hK1 (h.trans (Nat.gcd_dvd_right 3 _)))`.
- S267BadExcHRConc and S267BadExcHRConcB: `center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup_E6 hp hperf hcore eX hK5 (not_dvd_of_dvd_three hp hp5 (Nat.gcd_dvd_left 3 _))`.
- S267BadExcFldConc: the same call as in HRConc.
- S267BadExcFldModelA: `center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup_E6 hp hperf hcore eX hK5 (fun h => hpK1 (h.trans (Nat.gcd_dvd_right 3 _)))`.

The lemma needs no new imports, because HRConc already uses `e6_hopfMultiplier`. Each call site keeps its own hypotheses.
findings.benefit: Each of the five proofs loses a five-line nested `by` block and keeps only the divisibility argument specific to it. The Hopf-multiplier cardinality computation then lives in one place, so a change to the multiplier API or to `center_eq_bot_of_adjointGroup` needs one edit. The new name also states the fact being used, namely that the center of S is trivial because the E6 multiplier has order gcd(3, |K|-1) and p does not divide it.
